parts.stem:
The house mouse, *Mus musculus*, has a diploid number of 40 chromosomes.
Fig. 2.1 shows 6 of these chromosomes.

Fig. 2.1
parts.text: Identify **one** pair of homologous chromosomes on Fig. 2.1 by drawing circles around **two** chromosomes.

parts.label: (b)
(b)(i)
parts.text: Explain why chromosomes, such as those in Fig. 2.2, are described as a homologous pair.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: State the number of chromosomes that are present in *M. musculus* spermatozoa.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem:
*M. musculus* produces gametes by meiosis. These gametes are genetically different.
There is random fusion of gametes at fertilisation.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Explain why meiosis is important in the life cycle of *M. musculus*, **apart from** producing genetically different gametes.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Explain how the random fusion of gametes leads to the expression of rare, recessive alleles.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: A mutation causing coats of mice to be woolly in appearance is in a gene located on chromosome 11. The mutation causes a very shortened polypeptide product. Mice with the woolly coat phenotype have longer fur than mice with normal coats.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text: Explain how a base substitution mutation can lead to a very shortened polypeptide product.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.stem: The inheritance of the woolly coat characteristic was investigated.
